When our founding team was building a Farm Management System, we needed to create a crop protection planning tool with automated compliance auditing. Like everyone else, we looked to the historic industry standard for the data. The problem was immediate. The data was recorded in a way that relied heavily on narrative text to explain complex restrictions. As any developer knows, you cannot programmatically validate legality against a paragraph of text. You need structured, boolean logic. We realised that if it was this hard to build our FMS with the existing data, it was the same for everyone else. We pivoted. Leveraging advanced AI to parse and structure authorisation documents, we built a proprietary engine that turns regulatory noise into clean JSON. CodeCraft IT provides specialised software consulting and development services to organisations of any size. We have skills in enterprise Java development, as well as Ruby on Rails. Our team takes pride in delivering beautiful, quality code that does just what you need it to! Our Mission To create beautiful software that we are proud of, and that does just what it needs to. To always strive to improve ourselves, and to share that knowledge and experience with our clients to improve the software skills set of our industry. Where We Fit In Software development is often seen as a sub-function of the business analysis function. This results in the unique responsibilities of this discipline often being downplayed. As a consequence they often produce software solutions that are lower quality, difficult to manage in production, and harder to maintain and modify to meet the business’s changing needs. At CodeCraft IT, we believe that the three tensions of software delivery – time/cost, functionality and quality – are, or should be, the responsibilities of three distinct groups. Time/cost is the responsibility of the project managers who ensure that projects are completed on schedule and within budget. Functionality is the responsibility of the business through business analysts, who ensure that business needs drive the software requirements, not the other way round. Quality is the responsibility of the developers, who must make sure that the software is fit for purpose, well designed, and maintainable
